newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH AGROBANKA SAYS NEEDS CZK 8.7 BLN IN RESERVES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH AGROBANKA SAYS NEEDS CZK 8.7 BLN IN RESERVES.

text.p: The troubled Czech Agrobanka a.s., said on Thursday it needs to increase reserves by 8.7 billion crowns to cover potential losses accumulated through mid-September 1996, when it was put under central bank administration.

"The audit put the need for reserves and provisions at 8.7 billion crowns," Agrobanka spokesman Vlastimil Nesrsta told Reuters. He said a complete audit by Price Waterhouse for 1996, would be completed by the end of March.
The bank had said earlier that its need for additional reserves would be just six billion crowns, added to the four billion it already had.

Agrobanka is the fifth largest Czech bank, and the largest fully private financial institution in the country in terms of assets. It had a 372 million crown net profit in 1995, after 171 million in 1994.
It was put under a forced administration of the Czech National Bank (CNB) in September after a liquidity crisis threatened the bank.
Central bank officials have said Agrobanka's loss for 1996 would be "in the billions" of crowns.
The CNB chose the London office of HSBC Investment Bank to conduct a tender looking for a strategic investor to take over a controlling stake in the bank.
